title: http: compare query parameter keys and preserve present empty values
body:
Audit finding 1: **High — HTTP query lookup compares key length but not key content**

Verified against `edva 1.1.1+b8e2267`, source revision `b8e22672040b588151848e4483d3ebda97fdeb08`, on 2026-10-13. [Full audit report](https://github.com/edva-lang/edva/blob/master/audits/2026-10-13-rerun/report.md). Issues are tracked in Gitea; source and reproductions are hosted on GitHub.

At [std/net/http.dva](https://github.com/edva-lang/edva/blob/b8e22672040b588151848e4483d3ebda97fdeb08/std/net/http.dva), lines 292–310, `query_param` looks for `=` at the requested key's length but never compares the preceding bytes with `key`.

[Reproduction](https://github.com/edva-lang/edva/blob/master/audits/2026-10-13-rerun/reproductions/http_query_key/probe.dva):

| Call | Expected | Actual |
|---|---|---|
| `query_param("x=1&y=2", "y")` | `"2"` | `"1"` |
| `query_param("role=user&name=admin", "name")` | `"admin"` | `"user"` |
| `query_param("x=1", "z")` | absent | present |
| `query_param("x=", "x")` | present empty value | absent |

This can select an unrelated application parameter. Compare the full key before accepting a segment, and track whether a match occurred separately from the output length. Define duplicate-key and decoding behavior explicitly.

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] Assert all four reported query lookups; define duplicate-key and decoding behavior.
- [ ] Add regression coverage appropriate to this finding and update affected contracts/reference text.

title: http: parse Content-Length with correct field boundaries and numeric validation
body:
Audit finding 2: **High — Content-Length extraction misreads valid headers and accepts unrelated or invalid ones**

Verified against `edva 1.1.1+b8e2267`, source revision `b8e22672040b588151848e4483d3ebda97fdeb08`, on 2026-10-13. [Full audit report](https://github.com/edva-lang/edva/blob/master/audits/2026-10-13-rerun/report.md). Issues are tracked in Gitea; source and reproductions are hosted on GitHub.

At [std/net/http.dva](https://github.com/edva-lang/edva/blob/b8e22672040b588151848e4483d3ebda97fdeb08/std/net/http.dva), lines 376–384, `content_length` performs a case-sensitive substring search and skips a fixed 16 bytes. It neither parses a complete field name nor validates the entire numeric value.

[Reproduction](https://github.com/edva-lang/edva/blob/master/audits/2026-10-13-rerun/reproductions/http_content_length/probe.dva):

| Header | Actual |
|---|---|
| `Content-Length: 12` | 12, control |
| `Content-Length:12` | **2**, first digit skipped |
| `content-length: 12` | absent |
| `X-Content-Length: 12` | incorrectly present |
| `Content-Length: invalid` | present value **0** |

HTTP field names are case-insensitive and whitespace after the colon is optional. [RFC 9112 §5](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9112.html#section-5). Incorrect length selection affects where the parser believes a request ends; interoperability and connection synchronization are at risk. No end-to-end request-smuggling exploit was attempted.

Parse complete header lines, normalize field-name comparison, trim permitted whitespace, and validate nonnegative decimal length with overflow and duplicate-field checks. Return a distinct invalid-header result rather than treating malformed input as zero or absent.

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] Cover case-insensitive names, zero/optional whitespace, unrelated field names, malformed values, overflow, and duplicate lengths.
- [ ] Add regression coverage appropriate to this finding and update affected contracts/reference text.

title: http: reject incomplete bodies and unsupported framing instead of returning success
body:
Audit finding 3: **High — HTTP request reading reports success for incomplete or unsupported body framing**

Verified against `edva 1.1.1+b8e2267`, source revision `b8e22672040b588151848e4483d3ebda97fdeb08`, on 2026-10-13. [Full audit report](https://github.com/edva-lang/edva/blob/master/audits/2026-10-13-rerun/report.md). Issues are tracked in Gitea; source and reproductions are hosted on GitHub.

At [std/net/http.dva](https://github.com/edva-lang/edva/blob/b8e22672040b588151848e4483d3ebda97fdeb08/std/net/http.dva), lines 387–440, `read_body` breaks on `recv <= 0` and returns any bytes accumulated. `read_req_body` converts absence into an empty string, and `request_method` returns success unconditionally after reading headers/body.

- [Truncated-body probe](https://github.com/edva-lang/edva/blob/master/audits/2026-10-13-rerun/reproductions/http_truncated_body/probe.dva): send a request declaring ten body bytes, supply `abc`, then shut down the sender. `read_request` returns a successful request with a **three-byte** body.
- [Chunked-body probe](https://github.com/edva-lang/edva/blob/master/audits/2026-10-13-rerun/reproductions/http_chunked_body/probe.dva): send a valid chunked body containing `abc`. `read_request` succeeds with a **zero-byte** body; the chunk framing remains unread.

A body shorter than its declared Content-Length is incomplete. Chunked framing requires its own decoding and completion checks. [RFC 9112 §§6.3, 7.1, 8](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9112.html#section-6.3).

Carry completion/error status through all helper layers. Either implement chunked requests or explicitly reject them and close the connection. Also define and enforce separate request-line, aggregate-header, and body limits: current `max` is passed into line reads, while Content-Length directly determines body allocation. The allocation-limit concern is source review, not an exhaustion experiment.

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] Reject truncated declared bodies; decode or explicitly reject chunked requests; assert remaining-stream behavior and define bounded header/body allocation.
- [ ] Add regression coverage appropriate to this finding and update affected contracts/reference text.

title: io: finish partial-write and error handling in console output wrappers
body:
Audit finding 4: **High — Console writers still silently discard partial writes**

Verified against `edva 1.1.1+b8e2267`, source revision `b8e22672040b588151848e4483d3ebda97fdeb08`, on 2026-10-13. [Full audit report](https://github.com/edva-lang/edva/blob/master/audits/2026-10-13-rerun/report.md). Issues are tracked in Gitea; source and reproductions are hosted on GitHub.

The raw `io::write` repair works in the tested nonblocking case: it returns the bytes transferred. [Control](https://github.com/edva-lang/edva/blob/master/audits/2026-10-13-rerun/reproductions/io_write_count/probe.dva) reports **65,536 written and 65,536 received**, allowing callers to detect the short transfer.

However, `log`, `outs`, and `errs` still issue one `libc::writev` and discard its result at [std/io.dva](https://github.com/edva-lang/edva/blob/b8e22672040b588151848e4483d3ebda97fdeb08/std/io.dva):155, 271, and 282. `out` and `err` use that path; the formatted writer calls the improved raw helper but discards its return value too.

[Console-output probe](https://github.com/edva-lang/edva/blob/master/audits/2026-10-13-rerun/reproductions/io_out_partial/probe.dva): redirect stdout to a nonblocking pipe and call `io::out` with 100,000 characters. The call returns normally, but only **65,536 of the expected 100,001 bytes**, including newline, arrive. Pipe capacity varies by host; silent loss is the defect.

Define a common completion/backpressure contract for every writer. Handle EINTR, advance across partial vectors, and expose incomplete progress or a recoverable failure. Retrying EAGAIN in a tight loop is not sufficient. The documentation currently says EINTR is retried by `io` operations generally, which overstates these wrappers' behavior.

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] Preserve every byte or expose incomplete progress/failure for out, err, outs, errs, outf, and errf; test short writev, EINTR, EAGAIN, and permanent failure.
- [ ] Add regression coverage appropriate to this finding and update affected contracts/reference text.

Related completed work: #157. This follow-up isolates the remaining scope verified after those repairs.

title: io: clear stale would-block state on EOF and expose stdin reader status
body:
Audit finding 5: **Medium — `read_all` retains EAGAIN after clean EOF; `in` hides reader status entirely**

Verified against `edva 1.1.1+b8e2267`, source revision `b8e22672040b588151848e4483d3ebda97fdeb08`, on 2026-10-13. [Full audit report](https://github.com/edva-lang/edva/blob/master/audits/2026-10-13-rerun/report.md). Issues are tracked in Gitea; source and reproductions are hosted on GitHub.

[Status-transition probe](https://github.com/edva-lang/edva/blob/master/audits/2026-10-13-rerun/reproductions/io_readall_stale_status/probe.dva):

1. Read an empty nonblocking pipe while its writer is open: absence, errno 11.
2. Close the writer and call `read_all` again: absence, **EOF true, would-block true, errno still 11**.

The EOF branch at [std/io.dva](https://github.com/edva-lang/edva/blob/b8e22672040b588151848e4483d3ebda97fdeb08/std/io.dva):339–342 sets `r.eof` without clearing `r.err`. The separate `refill` implementation clears the error on EOF. `reader_would_block` promises to describe the last read, so the stale flag contradicts its contract and can misdirect readiness handling.

Use consistent state transitions across read paths and test EAGAIN → data, EAGAIN → EOF, and fatal error → recovery. Prefer one shared state-update helper.

An associated API omission remains in [std/in.dva](https://github.com/edva-lang/edva/blob/b8e22672040b588151848e4483d3ebda97fdeb08/std/in.dva): its reader is private and its public wrappers expose no error/EOF/would-block inspection. [The reference](https://github.com/edva-lang/edva/blob/b8e22672040b588151848e4483d3ebda97fdeb08/doc/reference/stdlib/in.qmd):13 still describes absence solely as EOF. Expose corresponding status accessors, or document this limitation and direct applications needing error distinction to `io::Reader`.

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] Test EAGAIN to data, EAGAIN to EOF, and error recovery across read paths; expose in status or explicitly document its limitation.
- [ ] Add regression coverage appropriate to this finding and update affected contracts/reference text.

Related completed work: #158. This follow-up isolates the remaining scope verified after those repairs.

title: json: preserve compensated decimal numbers across intermediate overflow and underflow
body:
Audit finding 6: **Medium — JSON loses representable numbers through intermediate overflow or underflow**

Verified against `edva 1.1.1+b8e2267`, source revision `b8e22672040b588151848e4483d3ebda97fdeb08`, on 2026-10-13. [Full audit report](https://github.com/edva-lang/edva/blob/master/audits/2026-10-13-rerun/report.md). Issues are tracked in Gitea; source and reproductions are hosted on GitHub.

The old `1e-309` failure is repaired. More extreme but representable final values still fail:

| JSON number constructed by the probe | Mathematical value | Parsed Float |
|---|---:|---:|
| `1` followed by 309 zeros, then `e-309` | 1 | infinity |
| `0.` followed by 399 zeros, then `1e400` | 1 | 0 |

[Reproduction](https://github.com/edva-lang/edva/blob/master/audits/2026-10-13-rerun/reproductions/json_compensated_number/probe.dva) also prints false for both comparisons with `1.0`.

[std/json.dva](https://github.com/edva-lang/edva/blob/b8e22672040b588151848e4483d3ebda97fdeb08/std/json.dva):174–186 accumulates the unscaled significand in a Float; lines 329–389 apply the exponent afterward. Once the significand becomes infinity or zero, later exponent adjustment cannot recover it. Clamping the exponent independently of the decimal position also prevents general correct conversion.

Use a decimal-to-binary conversion that combines significant digits and exponent before overflowing intermediate state. Alternatively, reject explicitly unsupported number forms with a documented error. Returning a successful, unrelated value is not a usable range-limit policy. Add tests for long mantissas whose final values are ordinary finite numbers.

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] Parse both reported compensated numbers as 1.0, or reject explicitly documented unsupported forms; retain correct normal/subnormal conversion.
- [ ] Add regression coverage appropriate to this finding and update affected contracts/reference text.

Related completed work: #153. This follow-up isolates the remaining scope verified after those repairs.

title: json: validate raw UTF-8 string bytes or expose an explicit checked parser contract
body:
Audit finding 7: **Medium — JSON accepts invalid raw UTF-8 in strings**

Verified against `edva 1.1.1+b8e2267`, source revision `b8e22672040b588151848e4483d3ebda97fdeb08`, on 2026-10-13. [Full audit report](https://github.com/edva-lang/edva/blob/master/audits/2026-10-13-rerun/report.md). Issues are tracked in Gitea; source and reproductions are hosted on GitHub.

[Reproduction](https://github.com/edva-lang/edva/blob/master/audits/2026-10-13-rerun/reproductions/json_invalid_utf8/probe.dva) constructs a quoted string containing byte `0xFF`. `json::parse` reports success.

The raw-character path in [std/json.dva](https://github.com/edva-lang/edva/blob/b8e22672040b588151848e4483d3ebda97fdeb08/std/json.dva):89–99 checks control characters, then copies bytes without validating UTF-8 sequences. The repaired `\u` escape path does not cover this route. Interoperable exchanged JSON uses UTF-8. [RFC 8259 §8.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8259.html#section-8.1).

Validate raw string sequences, including continuation bytes, overlong encodings, surrogate code points, and maximum scalar value. If parsing intentionally assumes previously validated bytes, make that precondition explicit and provide a checked entry point; the current reference advertises strict JSON without that qualification.

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] Test invalid lead/continuation bytes, overlong forms, surrogate code points, and out-of-range scalars alongside valid UTF-8 and escape sequences.
- [ ] Add regression coverage appropriate to this finding and update affected contracts/reference text.

Related completed work: #152. This follow-up isolates the remaining scope verified after those repairs.

title: docs: finish stdlib signature, example, and sorting-complexity corrections
body:
Audit finding 8: **Medium — Current Quarto references retain API, example, and performance discrepancies**

Verified against `edva 1.1.1+b8e2267`, source revision `b8e22672040b588151848e4483d3ebda97fdeb08`, on 2026-10-13. [Full audit report](https://github.com/edva-lang/edva/blob/master/audits/2026-10-13-rerun/report.md). Issues are tracked in Gitea; source and reproductions are hosted on GitHub.

| Current reference | Discrepancy |
|---|---|
| [net.qmd](https://github.com/edva-lang/edva/blob/b8e22672040b588151848e4483d3ebda97fdeb08/doc/reference/stdlib/net.qmd):45 | `net::close_fd` is documented as `Int => ()`; [implementation](https://github.com/edva-lang/edva/blob/b8e22672040b588151848e4483d3ebda97fdeb08/std/net.dva):285 returns `Int`. |
| [net.qmd](https://github.com/edva-lang/edva/blob/b8e22672040b588151848e4483d3ebda97fdeb08/doc/reference/stdlib/net.qmd):72 | `http::respond` argument three is called `headers`; [implementation](https://github.com/edva-lang/edva/blob/b8e22672040b588151848e4483d3ebda97fdeb08/std/net/http.dva):66–72 accepts a **content type** and generates its own headers. The different `response` function correctly accepts preformatted headers. |
| [sort.qmd](https://github.com/edva-lang/edva/blob/b8e22672040b588151848e4483d3ebda97fdeb08/doc/reference/stdlib/sort.qmd):11,33 | Still describes all helpers as quadratic insertion sort. Typed `ints`/`strings` now use hybrid merge sort; only `raw_sort_slots` retains the generic insertion path. |
| [sort.qmd](https://github.com/edva-lang/edva/blob/b8e22672040b588151848e4483d3ebda97fdeb08/doc/reference/stdlib/sort.qmd):22–31 | Current example calls undefined `print_int`. [Exact copied sample](https://github.com/edva-lang/edva/blob/master/audits/2026-10-13-rerun/reproductions/doc_sort_current/probe.dva) fails with **E3004**, followed by inference/compilation diagnostics. |
| [in.qmd](https://github.com/edva-lang/edva/blob/b8e22672040b588151848e4483d3ebda97fdeb08/doc/reference/stdlib/in.qmd):13,26 | Treats absence as EOF and retains undefined legacy `print` calls. The status omission is covered in finding 5; this sample was reviewed statically. |
| [math.qmd](https://github.com/edva-lang/edva/blob/b8e22672040b588151848e4483d3ebda97fdeb08/doc/reference/stdlib/math.qmd):76–77 | Names `math/geom` and `math/complex` without documenting their public signatures and contracts. |

The previous `io`, JSON, and `http::response` sample defects were substantially corrected; this list concerns current text. Update signature tables against source declarations and make self-contained examples executable.

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] Correct close_fd and respond signatures/contracts, repair sort/in examples, describe typed merge sort separately from raw insertion sort, and document math submodule APIs.
- [ ] Add regression coverage appropriate to this finding and update affected contracts/reference text.

Related completed work: #162, #166. This follow-up isolates the remaining scope verified after those repairs.

title: docs: validate partial-example exemptions, expected output, and LLM code snippets
body:
Audit finding 9: **Medium — Documentation validation improved, but exemptions and missing assertions still hide defects**

Verified against `edva 1.1.1+b8e2267`, source revision `b8e22672040b588151848e4483d3ebda97fdeb08`, on 2026-10-13. [Full audit report](https://github.com/edva-lang/edva/blob/master/audits/2026-10-13-rerun/report.md). Issues are tracked in Gitea; source and reproductions are hosted on GitHub.

The earlier silent omission of unclassified code blocks is fixed. The checker now requires classification, compiles complete examples, executes run examples, checks negative diagnostics, and fails when requested compilation lacks a compiler. The documentation CI job now requests compilation.

Remaining gaps in [tools/check_docs.nu](https://github.com/edva-lang/edva/blob/b8e22672040b588151848e4483d3ebda97fdeb08/tools/check_docs.nu):

- **77 blocks are classified as partial** and therefore excluded from compilation. Some are legitimate fragments; the complete-looking sort usage sample in finding 8 demonstrates that the exemption also hides broken examples. This is not a claim that all 77 should run unmodified.
- Run checks at lines 186–195 inspect exit status but do not assert output. Wrong successful results can pass; signatures containing interchangeable String parameters are particularly easy to misuse.
- Example discovery at line 83 covers `.qmd` files only. Dva examples in `doc/llms.txt` and `doc/llms-full.txt` are outside that compilation check; synchronized operator tables do not validate these examples.

Require a short reason or supporting context for partial examples, promote complete usage examples to run/complete, support expected-output assertions, and validate suitable LLM snippets with the same machinery. This preserves legitimate fragment documentation while making exclusions reviewable.

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] Require reviewable fragment exemptions, add expected-output assertions, and include suitable llms.txt/llms-full.txt examples in validation without breaking legitimate fragments.
- [ ] Add regression coverage appropriate to this finding and update affected contracts/reference text.

Related completed work: #164. This follow-up isolates the remaining scope verified after those repairs.

title: docs/llms: reconcile completeness claims with API coverage and parser state contracts
body:
Audit finding 10: **Medium — LLM instructions still promise a complete reference but provide only a library overview**

Verified against `edva 1.1.1+b8e2267`, source revision `b8e22672040b588151848e4483d3ebda97fdeb08`, on 2026-10-13. [Full audit report](https://github.com/edva-lang/edva/blob/master/audits/2026-10-13-rerun/report.md). Issues are tracked in Gitea; source and reproductions are hosted on GitHub.

[doc/llms.txt](https://github.com/edva-lang/edva/blob/b8e22672040b588151848e4483d3ebda97fdeb08/doc/llms.txt):5 and its full-reference link describe a complete standard-library reference; [doc/llms-full.txt](https://github.com/edva-lang/edva/blob/b8e22672040b588151848e4483d3ebda97fdeb08/doc/llms-full.txt):3 similarly promises completeness. Its library section at line 291 contains only six overview bullets, with no API reference for modules such as `sort`, `uring`, `color`, `fp`, or `type`.

The old false JSON streaming/serialization claim and the incomplete E3130 category description were corrected. The scope claim and API coverage remain unresolved. Neither the JSON reference nor these instructions now explains the parser's module-global `src`/`pos` state and associated reentrancy/threading assumptions; this is a missing contract, not a reproduced concurrent failure.

Either generate a comprehensive reference from the source inventory and maintained documentation, or accurately label the files as a curated language guide and provide module links. Keep error handling, partial progress, memory lifetime, and concurrency restrictions in the machine-readable material as well as the human-facing reference.

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] Provide comprehensive API coverage or accurately label and link a curated guide; document JSON parser reentrancy/threading assumptions and relevant I/O/lifetime contracts.
- [ ] Add regression coverage appropriate to this finding and update affected contracts/reference text.

Related completed work: #165. This follow-up isolates the remaining scope verified after those repairs.
